gen-dafont-quark-fs-trench-slab: Trench Slab reads dignified and refined, its caps barely rising above the lowercase. Quark sits against it with geometric, technical strokes that never thin, so the sans heading and the serif body feel like two different drafting hands.
gen-dafont-quark-manrope: Manrope reads bright and approachable, every curve left open at the mouth. Quark has the same unvarying line and geometric build, so the two blend easily, and a modest body size lets that spacious look breathe.
gen-dafont-quark-satoshi: Quark's strokes never vary, from stem to terminal, giving its geometric letters a technical hush. Satoshi follows with a soaring x-height and a wide-open e, and the two share enough build to look cut from one cloth.
gen-dafont-quark-work-sans: Work Sans reads contemporary and modern, with c tips held well apart and a mean line set high. Quark earns its keep big and short, where its spacious c and uniform line get room to show.
gen-dafont-radikal-fs-supreme: Supreme sets a thick, heavy-looking band through the middle of each line, with letters held open rather than curled shut. Radikal's wire-bent curves close up where Supreme opens out, and that tension is the point.
gen-dafont-radikal-manrope: Radikal comes in bold, its wire-bent s curves never thinning at the spine. Manrope answers by leaving every curved letter bright and open, so the plain sans body gives the heading room to stand out.
gen-dafont-radikal-satoshi: Satoshi stands tall on a soaring x-height, its e wide open and never squeezed. And Radikal, with its closed, wire-bent curves and generous gaps, makes a firmer, more guarded partner for all that openness.
gen-dafont-radikal-work-sans: Wire-bent s curves that never thin at the spine give Radikal a professional, bold spine of its own. Work Sans then reads contemporary and modern, its c tips held apart, so extended text on a page feels open after the closed heading.
gen-dafont-reckoner-fs-merriweather-sans: Reckoner feels like tracing one thick thread, with spacing clamped tight as a vise. Merriweather Sans loosens things with tall, sturdy lowercase and an e that opens clearly to the right.
gen-dafont-reckoner-fs-neco: Reckoner's single thick thread of a stroke, packed in tight, is what you notice first. Neco, a serif with a measured swell from hairline to stem, brings a dignified, authoritative note that the heading's constant line lacks.
